t: Three Maine towns put data center bans or pauses to voters
b: North Berwick skipped a moratorium to let voters decide on a permanent ban.
iw: Possible permanent bans

t: Archbald unanimously denies the 14-building Wildcat Ridge campus
b: The 578-acre plan included 588 diesel backup generators. After nine hearings, council rejected it; an appeal is expected. Four more campuses are proposed in the borough.
iw: Hyperscale campus denied

t: Somerset County requires data centers to make 150% of their own power
b: Unanimous ordinance also sets 1,000-foot setbacks from homes. No project had been filed.
iw: Very demanding power rule

t: Advocates count 110 New Jersey towns with data center bans
b: The group is pressing Gov. Sherrill for a three-year statewide moratorium.
iw: Breadth of local bans

t: South Berwick adopts a 180-day pause for facilities over 10,000 sq ft
b: Retroactive to July 14. It expires just before the state's recommendations are due Jan. 29, 2027.
iw: Low size threshold

t: State fines Vineland data center $1.07M for 62 unpermitted generators
b: DataOne must get permits within 45 days or stop running the gas generators. Regulators called it the largest enforcement action against a data center in the state.
iw: Enforcement against on-site power

t: Massena declines to adopt a data center moratorium
b: St. Lawrence County had urged its towns to consider pauses.
iw: Pause rejected

t: Harvie calls for a data center moratorium in his race against Fitzpatrick
b: A new TV ad in the Bucks County House race marks a shift in his position.
iw: Pause pledge in a swing district

t: Butternuts adopts a data center moratorium
b: Unanimous vote in Otsego County.
iw: Rural town pause

t: Brick introduces a ban; Bridgewater opts for rules
b: Bridgewater already doesn't permit data centers anywhere but avoided an outright ban over lawsuit concerns.
iw: More towns acting

t: Greenfield moves toward a one-year pause as more cities weigh limits
b: New Bedford is considering a ban; Northampton and Easthampton are eyeing moratoriums.
iw: More pauses likely

t: Minogue says Massachusetts can't handle more data center demand
b: Healey's Republican opponent shows little interest in new data centers either.
iw: Both candidates skeptical

t: House Democrats plan a 24-month moratorium bill for 2027
b: Announced the same day Ayotte said she opposes any data center in the state.
iw: Bipartisan appetite for a pause

t: Springhill Township bars new data center and power plant applications
b: A temporary ban while it writes setback and noise rules, prompted by interest in 800 acres near Gans.
iw: Temporary township ban

t: Lamont: Connecticut is the wrong place for massive AI data centers
b: He'd consider projects that bring their own power, pass utility regulators and win local approval. Earlier he urged the state to slow down new data centers.
iw: Governor discourages hyperscale projects

t: Fazio wants to end Connecticut's data center tax breaks
b: The Republican nominee opposes incentives but not an outright ban.
iw: Both candidates cool on incentives

t: Gorham moves toward a permanent data center ban
b: Councilors unanimously sent the proposal to the planning board; a temporary moratorium is already in place.
iw: Possible permanent ban

t: Hopkinton imposes a 60-day emergency pause
b: Unanimous, while the planning board drafts a permanent zoning amendment.
iw: Short emergency pause

t: Data centers must report water and energy use every six months
b: S3379 also came with state guidance for towns negotiating community benefits agreements. Advocates called it too weak and renewed calls for a moratorium.
iw: New disclosure duties

t: Orangetown pauses data centers and battery storage for six months
b: Residents objected that the pause doesn't reach DataBank's proposed second facility, already under environmental review near Lake Tappan.
iw: Pause, but the pending project is exempt

t: Judge blocks four new diesel generators at Lowell's data center
b: Residents challenged the state's air permit for eight more generators; four already installed can keep running.
iw: Court limits backup power expansion

t: Vineland weighs a revised 300 MW self-powered AI campus
b: The DataOne/Nebius plan would generate its own power; residents raised LNG storage, emissions, water and noise concerns.
iw: Large project still under review

t: More than 30 New Jersey towns ban data centers by mid-August
b: Includes Jersey City, Bayonne, Howell, Warren, Madison, East Brunswick and Stafford, per an advocacy group's count.
iw: Bans spreading statewide

t: Utility study eyes a large load at Bow's former coal plant
b: Eversource is studying service for a possible hyperscale project at the Merrimack Station site, per FERC filings. Gov. Ayotte opposes it.
iw: Early-stage project facing opposition

t: Westerly adopts a one-year data center moratorium
b: Voted 7–0 to study grid, water and emergency service impacts.
iw: One-year town pause

t: Brookhaven adopts an 18-month data center moratorium
b: Unanimous vote on Long Island two days after the state's executive order, aimed in part at a proposed Yaphank project.
iw: Long pause in a large suburban town

t: East Greenbush passes the first local pause after the state order
b: A six-month moratorium on data center development and operation in Rensselaer County.
iw: Six-month town pause

t: PJM's capacity auction hits the price cap again
b: The 2028/29 auction cleared at the $325/MW-day cap with a reserve shortfall. The market monitor attributes about 46% of capacity charges over four auctions to data centers.
iw: Mounting pressure to make data centers pay

t: New Jersey puts data centers in their own rate class
b: P.L.2026 c.32 covers new and existing data centers of 50 MW or more, requiring them to pay for their energy and grid upgrades and commit to 85% take-or-pay for ten years.
iw: Binding cost rules, including for existing sites

t: Seneca Nation and Sierra Club sue over the STAMP zoning agreement
b: The suit says a deal barring the Town of Alabama from changing its zoning without the county agency's approval is void. A $19.4 billion, 500 MW Stream campus is under review there.
iw: Could unwind the zoning a major campus relies on

t: New Haven considers a 12-month data center moratorium
b: A working group would recommend zoning standards within six months.
iw: Possible city pause

t: House votes 197–5 to repeal the data center sales tax break
b: The exemption is projected to cost $517 million a year by 2030. The Senate added similar language to a tax bill, and the House also passed a pause bill.
iw: Could end a major incentive

t: Healey stops accepting data center sales tax exemption applications
b: Paused the 2024 incentive and issued a framework of expectations on cost, water and community engagement, later made binding by Executive Order 658.
iw: Incentive paused indefinitely

t: Bethlehem adopts a one-year data center moratorium
b: The Albany County town acted before the statewide executive order.
iw: One-year town pause

t: All six Rhode Island data center bills die
b: Proposals on 30-year tax breaks, cost allocation, siting and water reporting were held for study. No statewide moratorium bill was filed.
iw: No incentives, no rules

t: American Tower withdraws East Greenwich application after a ban
b: The township banned data centers while the Mount Royal application was pending.
iw: Project withdrawn

t: West Haven adopts a one-year data center moratorium
b: Unanimous; incidental server rooms are exempt.
iw: One-year city pause

t: Developer sues Monroe Township for over $300 million over its ban
b: Moved to federal court in July. The outcome will signal how far New Jersey towns can go.
iw: Tests whether local bans hold

t: Allegany permanently bans data centers and crypto facilities
b: Local Law 3 applies in every zoning district. No project had been proposed; the board cited energy use and farmland loss.
iw: Permanent townwide ban

t: Frelinghuysen bans large data centers; Blairstown caps size at 5,000 sq ft
b: The county planning director says 18 of Warren County's 22 towns now have data center protections, many based on a county model ordinance.
iw: Most of a county now restrictive

t: Holyoke becomes the first Massachusetts city to ban AI data centers
b: A citywide ban, as other western Massachusetts cities weigh pauses.
iw: Citywide ban

t: Veto of Vermont's data center deployment bill is sustained
b: The House upheld the governor's veto of H.727 by 83–52, short of the votes needed to override.
iw: No new state framework

t: Sanford pauses data centers, stalling a 1,000-acre campus
b: A 91-day pause on the Sanford Woods campus along the Mousam River, later extended 180 days.
iw: Pause blocks a major proposal

t: Coalition asks Sherrill to use emergency powers for a moratorium
b: Cited rising bills, water use in the Pinelands aquifer and PFAS risks. She chose rules instead of a pause.
iw: Pressure for a state pause

t: S9144A would pause big data centers for three years
b: Covers facilities of 20 MW and up and asks regulators to keep costs off other ratepayers. Recommitted to committee in May; the narrower one-year bill passed instead.
iw: Longer statewide pause, stalled

t: Lysander adopts a six-month pause amid a 300 MW campus fight
b: Unanimous vote in Onondaga County following opposition to the proposed Ranalli campus. Several neighboring towns reportedly followed with one-year pauses.
iw: Pause aimed at a specific large project

t: Smithfield bans data centers in every zoning district
b: Passed 4–1, a day after Hanton City Investments filed for a complex near Fidelity's campus. The developer is appealing the town's incompleteness ruling.
iw: Townwide ban, contested

t: Oneonta pauses data centers and crypto mining for a year
b: Unanimous 12-month moratorium in Otsego County.
iw: One-year town pause

t: Townships use 180-day planning pauses to write data center rules
b: Pennsylvania towns can't ban a land use outright, so many use a curative amendment to pause applications while drafting ordinances.
iw: Short pauses spreading

t: Harrison Township adopts its own data center ban
b: One of several Gloucester County bans this spring.
iw: Township ban

t: Bills to end data center incentives and set large-load rules die
b: SB 245 stalled in Finance; HB 5469 died on the House calendar. No statewide moratorium was enacted.
iw: Status quo holds

t: Morris pauses data centers and battery storage
b: The posted text sets 12 months; some coverage describes two years.
iw: Town pause

t: Mansfield adopts the state's first comprehensive data center bylaw
b: Voted at annual town meeting in May.
iw: Detailed local rules

t: Monroe Township bans data centers in every zone
b: Effective May 13. The ordinance says no prior approval vests a right to build one, closing a warehouse-to-data-center conversion.
iw: Township-wide ban

t: Logan Township bans data centers townwide
b: Also blocks existing warehouses from converting, amid confusion over a Route 130 project.
iw: Township ban

t: Phillipsburg and Waterford ban data centers in all zones
b: Waterford cited its status as a Pinelands community.
iw: Town bans

t: Kenilworth's mayor defends CoreWeave's AI campus at the old Merck site
b: She says the redevelopment replaces lost tax revenue; packed council meetings followed.
iw: Local backing for a major project

t: FERC extends PJM's capacity price cap for two more auctions
b: Grew out of Shapiro's 2025 settlement with PJM. The next uncapped auction is May 2027.
iw: Caps consumer costs; data center rules unchanged

t: Archbald rejects an 18-building campus near Staback Park
b: Unanimous denial of Archbald 1 LLC's 400-acre application.
iw: Project denied

t: Over 200 pack a hearing against the $19.4B STAMP data center
b: Seneca citizens and neighbors urged the county agency to reject the campus and its roughly $1.46 billion tax break request.
iw: Organized opposition to a flagship project

t: PennFuture calls for a statewide data center moratorium
b: The environmental group says development should wait for rules on siting, water and clean energy.
iw: Organized push for a state pause

t: House kills a one-year statewide data center ban
b: HB 1265 was found inexpedient to legislate on a voice vote.
iw: Statewide ban rejected

t: Dryden makes data centers a prohibited use
b: Follows an 18-month moratorium the Tompkins County town adopted in July 2024 after a developer proposal.
iw: Permanent zoning prohibition

t: Pemberton becomes the first New Jersey town to ban data centers
b: The Burlington County ordinance prohibits building or operating them.
iw: Township ban

t: Prevailing wage now applies to data center construction
b: P.L.2025 c.335 covers projects of 5 MW or more starting on or after March 1, 2026.
iw: Higher construction costs

t: PJM governors and the White House issue joint principles
b: Called for affordability, reliability, market reform and a longer price cap.
iw: Regional pressure on large-load costs

t: East Fishkill pauses data centers for three years
b: Unanimous vote; the moratorium runs to July 1, 2029, one of the longest in the state.
iw: Three-year halt

t: DeWitt bars data center permits through 2027
b: The Onondaga County town's moratorium cites the state Senate's proposed three-year pause.
iw: Town pause through 2027

t: Olyphant halts new data centers for six months
b: Voted 4–3 while it drafts an ordinance, as proposals cluster across Lackawanna County.
iw: Six-month pause

t: Montgomery's data center ban challenged in court
b: E. Kahn Development Corp. sued over the ban on a former commercial site.
iw: Ban under legal challenge

t: Lowell pauses new or expanded data centers for a year
b: Home to the state's largest data center, Markley's former Prince Spaghetti site.
iw: One-year city pause

t: Westfield adopts a one-year moratorium on additional data centers
b: It doesn't immediately affect Servistar's proposed 274 MW, 10-building campus, which would be New England's largest.
iw: Pause, but the big project is outside it

t: Vermont's AI data center moratorium bill never leaves committee
b: S.205 would have paused AI data centers until July 2030.
iw: Statewide pause died

t: A wave of Maine towns pause data centers after the veto
b: Bangor, Brunswick, Westbrook, Gorham, Gray, Scarborough and Saco approved pauses of 91 to 180 days starting in May.
iw: Local pauses filling the state gap

t: Archbald creates four data center zoning districts over objections
b: Passed 4–2 with one abstention; no residents spoke in favor. The districts made the borough a magnet for proposals.
iw: Zoning opened land to data centers

t: Lewiston votes down a $300 million data center
b: Rejected after swift opposition. A $5 billion Wiscasset proposal was paused a month earlier.
iw: Project rejected

t: STAMP data center approval rescinded after a Seneca lawsuit
b: The Tonawanda Seneca Nation and Sierra Club sued over $472 million in tax breaks approved without full environmental review. The developer withdrew to propose a larger project.
iw: First approval undone, though a bigger plan followed

t: Pennsylvania's data center equipment sales tax exemption
b: Still in force, though Shapiro's August order ties new certifications to his GRID standards.
iw: Valuable incentive, now conditioned

t: Connecticut's 2021 data center tax incentive is still on the books
b: Offers 20- or 30-year sales and property tax waivers for large investments. Only one company has used it.
iw: Generous incentive, little used

t: Loudoun's final vote on its 12-month pause moves to Nov. 17
b: Deferred from Oct. 20 so staff can gather more information. The pause would be retroactive to Sept. 15; 33 data center and substation applications are active.
iw: Pause in the densest data center market

t: Loudoun campus on 342 forested acres is deferred indefinitely
b: The applicant pulled its board hearing after the planning commission unanimously recommended denial.
iw: Project stalled

t: Leesburg march calls for a statewide data center moratorium
b: Part of a series of rallies organized with the Chesapeake Climate Action Network.
iw: Organized pressure for a state pause

t: Spanberger rules out a statewide data center moratorium
b: She called local pauses a local choice and pointed to her cost rules instead.
iw: No state pause

t: Spotsylvania backs a call for a statewide moratorium
b: Supervisors voted 4–2 to support Sen. Glen Sturtevant's request to the governor. Eight data centers are in the works in the county.
iw: Local pressure for a state pause

t: Moratorium bills stack up for Virginia's 2027 session
b: SB 843 from Sens. Perry and Roem would block data center permits from July 2027 to July 2030. Del. Shin and Sen. Sturtevant have their own versions.
iw: Possible statewide pause in 2027

t: QTS terminates the 2,100-acre Digital Gateway near Manassas
b: A judge voided the rezonings in 2025 over flawed hearing notices, and an appeals court agreed in March.
iw: Largest proposed corridor killed

t: Project Flash campus in Franklin County is cancelled
b: Developer talks failed after more than 40 speakers opposed it.
iw: Project cancelled

t: Christiansburg ends by-right data centers
b: Voted 6–0 to require conditional use permits in industrial zones.
iw: Slower approvals

t: Fauquier planners recommend denying a 900 MW Remington campus
b: The developers of the six-building project are now asking the town of Remington to annex the land.
iw: Large project in trouble

t: Federal suit over Amazon's Louisa site moves forward
b: A neighbor alleges brown tap water, dust and noise from the Northeast Creek campus.
iw: Litigation risk

t: Warner's first reelection ad focuses on data centers
b: He now says data centers need to cover their own costs, after earlier calling them a local issue.
iw: Senior Democrat turns critical

t: Data Center Fair Share Act would tie highway funds to data center tariffs
b: States would need tariffs making data centers cover their own energy infrastructure.
iw: Federal cost pressure

t: West Virginia law strips local control over certified data centers
b: HB 2014 lets the state certify microgrid districts and high-impact data centers, bars local zoning, noise and building rules for them, and sends most new property tax to the state.
s: WV Energy and Data Center Tracker
iw: Local governments can't block certified projects

t: Lawmakers approve certification rules for microgrids and data centers
b: HB 4983 makes developers flag projects that would place an inordinate burden on neighbors. A transparency amendment was voted down.
iw: Fast-track framework stays intact

t: Bill to restore local control over data centers stalls
b: SB 658, backed by Tucker County residents, never moved. Leaders said changes were premature.
iw: Preemption survives

t: State promises a citizen advisory council at a Tucker County forum
b: More than 150 people attended the panel near a proposed Fundamental Data campus and gas plant.
iw: Process, not new limits

t: Court dismisses Mingo County residents' suit over data center power plants
b: Residents challenged two TransGas facilities planned to power data centers near Holden and Wharncliffe.
iw: Legal challenge fails

t: Beshear order bars passing data center costs to other ratepayers
b: Executive Order 2026-494 also lets agencies deny permits on water and air grounds and expects full tax payment. Local approval is still up to communities.
iw: New cost and permit conditions

t: Kentucky data center guardrails stripped on the session's last day
b: Rep. Josh Bray's cost protections were removed from SB 197; LG&E/KU opposed them. A Democratic tariff bill also died.
iw: No statutory cost rules

t: Kentucky offers a 50-year sales tax exemption for data center equipment
b: Passed in 2025 and championed by Senate President Robert Stivers.
iw: Very long incentive

t: Regulators approve a mandatory data center rate class for co-ops
b: EKPC's tariff requires PSC approval of each data center contract. The PSC also approved $3 billion in LG&E/KU gas plants for expected data centers.
iw: Cost rules plus new supply

t: Meta revealed behind a 1.2 GW Mason County campus
b: A think tank estimates the project could get about $50 million a year in tax breaks. Residents had objected to secrecy.
iw: Major project under scrutiny

t: Oldham County's moratorium drove off a hyperscale developer
b: The company scrapped its project after the pause; the county later extended it.
iw: Project abandoned

t: Meade County and Franklin reject data center rezonings
b: Both votes were unanimous.
iw: Projects denied

t: Memphis rejects an 18-month pause, then passes a 135-day one
b: The longer moratorium failed 6–6 after weeks of protests. The shorter pause comes with land-use standards; xAI's Colossus expansion drove the fight.
iw: Short pause in a major hub

t: Memphis mayor orders a data center rules plan within 90 days
b: Shelby County commissioners are weighing competing regulations and a 12-month moratorium.
iw: Rules coming

t: Tennessee makes big data centers pay for grid upgrades, but lets them self-power
b: Public Chapter 961 covers facilities of 50 MW and up. It also allows on-site generation or independent power producers with little state oversight.
iw: Cost rule plus freedom to self-generate

t: Tennessee bills on permits and usage reporting fail
b: Including a proposal requiring large facilities to devote half their computing to public benefit.
iw: No new state limits

t: McMinnville adopts an 18-month data center moratorium
b: Unanimous, as a 25 MW gas-and-diesel-powered project was proposed. Coffee County passed its own pause the same night.
iw: Long rural pause

t: Rutherford County committee backs a six-month pause
b: Contingent on legal review and full commission approval.
iw: Possible county pause

t: Montgomery County advances data center setbacks and limits
b: Approved 17–4: 500-foot residential setbacks plus noise, site size and utility capacity rules, returning in November.
iw: New siting limits

t: TVA approves up to 300 MW for xAI's Memphis operations
b: The federal utility serves most of Tennessee, which limits the state's say over rates.
iw: Power secured for a major campus

t: Mississippi permits 41 permanent gas turbines for xAI in Southaven
b: Unanimous, three weeks after a hearing where residents uniformly opposed it. Advocates appealed in April.
iw: Permanent power approved

t: NAACP sues xAI over unpermitted turbines in Southaven
b: The Clean Air Act suit seeks to stop the turbines and fines up to $124,426 a day. The state calls them temporary mobile units.
iw: Litigation over on-site power

t: Judge lets the NAACP's xAI turbine case proceed
b: The Justice Department had asked the court to dismiss it. The ruling doesn't decide whether xAI broke the law.
iw: Case survives

t: Southaven neighbors file a class action over turbine noise
b: Alleges near-constant noise, vibration and property harm.
iw: Nuisance litigation

t: State sets a schedule to retire xAI's 69 temporary turbines
b: Retirements begin Aug. 18, but some units can run until July 2027.
iw: Phase-out with extensions

t: Southaven approves another SpaceXAI data center
b: The company's fifth in the Memphis area.
iw: Project approved

t: Jackson pauses data center approvals
b: Covers a 230-acre Saxum proposal, with an airport-area exception.
iw: Capital city pause

t: Mississippi's Amazon law gives data centers sweeping breaks
b: Passed in two days: large tax breaks, eased utility permitting and confidential negotiated rates.
iw: Strong incentives

t: Alabama's data center cost law takes effect
b: Act 2026-610 requires regulators to find that contracts for data centers of 150 MW and up cover their full cost and benefit other customers.
iw: Cost test for big contracts

t: Alabama regulators must vote publicly on big data center contracts
b: A vote is due within 90 days or the contract is deemed approved. Alabama Power must publish summaries; earlier filings redacted key terms.
iw: More scrutiny of deals

t: Bessemer rezones about 700 acres for 1,200 MW Project Marvel
b: Approved 5–2 for a QTS campus; the mayor and city attorney had signed nondisclosure agreements.
iw: Huge campus approved

t: Two Bessemer council members who backed Project Marvel lose their seats
b: A third was forced into a runoff and the mayor, who signed an NDA, faces one too.
iw: Voters punish approvals

t: Birmingham pauses data centers over 20 MW for six months
b: Unanimous; DC Blox and the Nebius AI factory are exempt.
iw: Big-city pause

t: Homewood, Cullman, Leeds and Fort Payne pause data centers
b: Springville and Morgan County followed in June and July.
iw: Local pauses spreading

t: Alabama counties ask for zoning power over data centers
b: Most counties can't zone, so rural projects need no local vote. The group wants the legislature to act in 2027.
iw: Push for local control

t: Georgia Power can charge big data centers for upstream grid costs
b: The rule covers new customers over 100 MW. Kemp has cited it in opposing new statutes.
iw: Higher connection costs

t: Regulators approve nearly 10,000 MW of new plants for data center growth
b: About 80% is expected to serve data centers.
iw: Supply for new campuses

t: Kemp vetoed a two-year pause on data center tax breaks
b: HB 1192 would have suspended the sales tax exemption. The breaks remain.
iw: Incentive preserved

t: Georgia's data center sales tax exemption now costs a projected $2.5B a year
b: Created in 2018 and running through 2031, the estimate is up 664% from an earlier $327 million.
iw: Large incentive in force

t: Senate votes 32–21 to repeal data center tax breaks; House never acts
b: SB 410 from Sen. Matt Brass died without a House hearing.
iw: Repeal failed

t: House passes a data center cost-shield bill 159–5; it doesn't become law
b: Critics said HB 1063 mostly codified the PSC's existing rule.
iw: Status quo holds

t: Bills for 2027 include a statewide pause and an end to tax breaks
b: One would pause construction through 2028; others would repeal or move up the exemption's expiration.
iw: Renewed pressure in 2027

t: Bulloch County rejects an outright ban 4–3 but keeps its pause
b: The moratorium runs through Dec. 31 while the county writes regulations.
iw: Pause continues

t: DeKalb extends its data center moratorium again
b: In place since 2025, it was extended another 100 days.
iw: Repeated extensions

t: Augusta extends its pause, but QTS's campus stays exempt
b: The original 49-day pause was extended 60 days with three public hearings.
iw: Pause with a big carve-out

t: Duke, regulators' staff and tech giants settle on a large-load tariff
b: Would cover customers of 50 MW and up at high load factors, or 150 MW at any. Amazon, Google, Microsoft and Meta signed; it needs NCUC approval.
iw: Upfront connection costs

t: Regulators deny a Duke gas turbine, citing uncertain data center demand
b: Voted 2–1 against the 255 MW unit at Hamlet, calling its costs certain and its need uncertain.
iw: Supply buildout slowed

t: Charlotte adopts a 150-day moratorium, the largest US city to do so
b: Voted 11–0; approved projects are exempt.
iw: Big-city pause

t: Charlotte's moratorium expires unless extended
b: City staff recommended extending it after a survey found 78% community opposition.
iw: Likely extension

t: Raleigh pauses approvals for data centers over 5 MW
b: Voted 7–1; Beaufort County adopted a one-year pause the same week.
iw: Capital city pause

t: Forsyth County rejects a six-month moratorium
b: Voted 5–2 after the county attorney warned of litigation, pointing to the challenge that undid Chatham County's pause.
iw: Pause rejected

t: Forsyth denies rezoning for the Project Iron Spur campus
b: Voted 5–2 against the 129-acre hyperscale site in Rural Hall.
iw: Project denied

t: Greensboro pauses data centers over 10 MW for 180 days
b: Voted 8–0; runs through Feb. 14, 2027.
iw: City pause

t: Alamance County adopts a one-year pause on 10 MW projects
b: Unanimous, after it grew from a six-month proposal.
iw: County pause

t: Durham County pauses large data centers through May 2027
b: Voted 4–1, aligning with the city; small closed-loop projects without diesel generators are exempt.
iw: Nine-month pause

t: Statesville and Waxhaw adopt data center pauses
b: Statesville's 180-day pause exempts the existing Compass project; Waxhaw adopted 12 months in August.
iw: Town pauses

t: Mountain counties and towns pause data centers
b: Clay, Madison, Swain and Watauga counties and Boone, Brevard, Clyde, Canton and Hendersonville have adopted moratoriums.
iw: Regional wave

t: Chatham County's moratorium is undone by a developer's challenge
b: The one-year pause froze a 750 MW Eco TIP West project, which sued.
iw: Court limits local pauses

t: Stokes and Davidson counties reject data center pauses
b: Stokes advanced the Project Delta rezoning instead.
iw: Pauses rejected

t: Lee County permits a 90 MW CyrusOne data center
b: The county says the project is vested and offered no incentives.
iw: Project proceeds

t: Datacenter Transparency Act would pause siting permits for two years
b: Covers facilities of 100 MW and up from August 2026 to August 2028; referred to the Rules Committee.
iw: Statewide pause proposal

t: Boone signs an agreement with Lightedge for a possible data center
b: A step toward hosting a facility in a region full of pauses.
iw: Local welcome

t: South Carolina's 2025 energy law adds data center ratepayer protections
b: Meant to keep data center costs off other customers.
iw: Cost protections

t: South Carolina's data center permitting and moratorium bills die
b: S.867 and S.902 never reached a floor vote, and moratorium bills H.5526 and H.5286 stalled.
iw: No state rules

t: Spartanburg County freezes data centers over 65 MW for a year
b: Passed 5–1; the Valara project already approved is unaffected.
iw: County pause with a high threshold

t: Self-powered Spartanburg data center isn't subject to power plant rules
b: The ruling covers the $2.8 billion project at a former Kohler plant.
iw: Lighter rules for self-power

t: TigerDC withdraws its Spartanburg incentive request after pushback
b: Residents had opposed property tax breaks for the project.
iw: Project withdrawn

t: Settlement bans data centers in most of Colleton's ACE Basin
b: Resolves a lawsuit over a 1,000 MW, 859-acre proposal. The county had adopted a six-month moratorium in July.
iw: Large area closed to data centers

t: Chesterfield and Newberry counties pause data centers
b: Newberry first voted down a land sale to a developer; Greenwood County began its own 12-month pause.
iw: County pauses

t: Florida utilities file data center rates under the new state law
b: FPL says its rates already comply, with 20-year contracts and full payment for new generation. Tampa Electric filed a new tariff; Duke's is under review.
iw: Strict cost terms

t: Florida's 2025 tax package rolls back the data center sales tax exemption
b: Part of HB 7031.
iw: Incentive reduced

t: 68% of Florida voters oppose an AI data center in their community
b: Only 28% support one, with energy, bills, noise and water the top concerns.
iw: Strong opposition

t: Donalds favors local approvals with strict protections
b: His Democratic opponent, David Jolly, pledges a statewide one-year moratorium.
iw: Conditional support

t: Volusia County bans data centers of 50 MW or more
b: Applies in unincorporated areas, citing the aquifer and sinkholes. Smaller projects face extra review.
iw: Permanent county ban

t: Broward County moves toward a one-year moratorium
b: Unanimous vote to begin the process for unincorporated areas.
iw: Likely county pause

t: Wakulla County bans data centers outright
b: Unanimous, for unincorporated areas.
iw: County ban

t: North Port adopts an 18-month data center moratorium
b: Passed 3–2, exempting a roughly 900,000-square-foot project already proposed.
iw: Long city pause

t: Marion County pauses data centers of 50 MW or more for a year
b: Alachua County's planning commission backed a similar 12-month pause the same day.
iw: County pause

t: Edgewater enacts a permanent ban on data centers and crypto mining
b: Unanimous, ahead of a Nov. 3 vote to write it into the city charter.
iw: Permanent city ban

t: Levy and Putnam counties pause large data centers
b: Levy's moratorium runs Oct. 1 to Sept. 30, 2027, citing reliance on the Floridan Aquifer.
iw: County pauses

t: Sarasota County and Lakeland adopt one-year pauses
b: Lakeland's took effect after a final reading Aug. 3.
iw: Local pauses

t: Clay, Hernando and Lake counties adopt one-year moratoriums
b: Approved the same day.
iw: County pauses

t: Jackson County pauses AI data centers before any are proposed
b: A one-year pause to research impacts and draft rules.
iw: Preemptive county pause

t: Tallahassee rejects an AI data center ban 3–2
b: Commissioners said existing zoning already excludes such facilities.
iw: Ban rejected, zoning already restrictive

t: Indiantown and Taylor County reject data center pauses
b: Indiantown's council voted 4–1 and fired its village manager the same night.
iw: Pauses rejected

t: Escambia County bans large data centers and targets mid-size ones
b: A July resolution barred them as principal uses and an August ban covered large facilities. A pause on 10 to 50 MW projects is in the works.
iw: County ban

t: Louisiana offers 20-year data center sales tax relief
b: Act 730 sets a low bar of $200 million and 50 jobs, stacked with parish deals.
iw: Generous incentive

t: Regulators approve three gas plants for Meta's Hyperion campus
b: Built for Meta in Richland Parish over substantial community pushback.
iw: Dedicated supply approved

t: Louisiana fast-tracks power plants for large loads
b: An executive order led regulators to adopt the Lightning Amendment, which skips the usual least-cost review.
iw: Faster approvals

t: Regulators fast-track seven more gas plants for Meta's expansion
b: About 5.3 GW in Richland and Pointe Coupee parishes. A consumer group estimates data center growth could add $26 billion in system costs.
iw: More supply likely

t: Regulators vote 3–1 to keep Meta's data center details secret
b: Overturned a judge's subpoena for how Meta calculated its jobs and power needs. The vote split along party lines.
iw: Less disclosure

t: Entergy discloses Meta will use 4,500 MW as hearing opens
b: Entergy has a settlement with regulators' staff; opponents say ratepayers could be left with plant costs after Meta's 20-year contract.
iw: Approval expected

t: Landry says Louisiana doesn't need a moratorium
b: He favors what he calls responsible growth as other states clamp down.
iw: Pro-development stance

t: New Orleans bars data centers until mid-2027
b: An interim zoning ban; Caddo Parish has twice rejected a pause.
iw: City ban

t: Two Louisiana PSC seats are on the ballot
b: The commission will rule on Hyperion's second phase and large-load tariff policy.
iw: Regulator makeup at stake

t: Arkansas's Act 851 limits how cities can restrict data centers
b: Written mostly for crypto mining; Little Rock's mayor says it means cities can't ban data centers.
iw: Limits local bans

t: Little Rock adopts data center zoning rules
b: Defines hyperscale as over 250,000 square feet or 75 MW. Residents wanted a moratorium on a proposed Google project.
iw: Rules, not a pause

t: Little Rock rejects a data center moratorium on a 4–4 tie again
b: A six-month pause failed by the same vote as an 18-month one in August.
iw: Pause rejected

t: Pulaski County rejects a 12-month moratorium
b: Voted 10–3 amid disputes over exempting AVAIO's $6 billion Wrightsville project.
iw: Pause rejected

t: Pulaski County judge vetoes data center rules
b: The quorum court passed conditional-use rules 11–4; an override needs nine votes.
iw: Rules blocked for now

t: Pulaski County may vote to override the veto
b: The rules would require conditional use permits, setbacks and noise caps with no AVAIO carve-out.
iw: Possible new rules

t: Independence County adopts a five-year moratorium
b: Runs through Aug. 31, 2031, citing water supply strain; no project had been proposed.
iw: Very long pause

t: Madison County adopts a three-year moratorium
b: Voted 8–0; Union and Carroll counties adopted one-year pauses in June and Russellville six months in July.
iw: Long pause

t: Lawmakers grill Entergy over charging ratepayers for Google-linked solar
b: A rider covers Cypress Solar for Google's West Memphis campus. A judge rejected Entergy's bid to stop a newspaper publishing its Google agreements.
iw: Scrutiny of cost shifting

t: Littleton weighs six-month moratorium on new data centers
b: The ordinance had a first reading in October. A public hearing and second reading are planned for Nov. 3. Staff would study land-use, energy, water, noise and infrastructure impacts.
iw: Possible pause if adopted, not yet decided

t: Aurora to vote on indefinite data center moratorium after neighbors protest Trident project
b: A mayor-backed proposal would stop new applications until regulations are adopted but would not affect the pending Trident project. The Oct. 19 vote was delayed to Oct. 26 because two supporters could not attend.
iw: Indefinite pause on new applications in a major metro city

w: Missoula County Planning, Development and Sustainability
t: Missoula County study finds data center risks justify its moratorium
b: The draft emergency study released Oct. 21 cites electricity demand and costs, noise, wildlife and residential compatibility, and recommends stronger zoning. The county may extend the pause past July 8, 2027. A permanent ban is unlikely under the Right to Compute Act.
iw: Points to stricter zoning and a possible second year of pause

t: Colorado PUC holds public hearing on Xcel's large-load data center tariff
b: The commission heard public comment on Xcel's proposal to make very large power users cover the grid costs of serving them. Five days earlier, activists delivered a petition with almost 5,000 signatures urging stronger customer protections.
iw: Tariff would shift grid costs onto large users like data centers

t: Brighton adopts one-year data center moratorium on second reading
b: After a first-reading vote Oct. 6, the day after a developer withdrew a 2.5-million-square-foot rezoning application, the council approved the ordinance again Oct. 20, the Denver Gazette reports. The pause runs one year from its effective date and can be extended 90 days. The effective date is unconfirmed.
iw: New applications frozen for a year in a growing metro city

t: Hearing on Project Jupiter's air permit set for Dec. 7 in Sunland Park
b: Hearing Officer James Browning, a retired federal judge, scheduled the hearing to begin Dec. 7, with the first day for public comment. He also set Oct. 26 and Oct. 29 sessions on a motion to dismiss and on discovery.
iw: Key power-source permit decision still months away

t: Stratos developer files new water-right application with Utah regulators
b: O'Leary Digital asked the state to move existing irrigation water rights to the Stratos campus, saying use would fall below current farm use. A 20-day protest period follows public advertising. Two earlier applications were withdrawn after heavy protests.
iw: Necessary water step, but protests are expected

t: Attorney general says substantial share of Project Jupiter permit comments were not genuine
b: Torrez reviewed 17,419 comments: about 60% were one pro-project form letter from roughly 9,000 internet addresses, mostly with out-of-state phone numbers. About 4,700, mostly opposed, came from 17 connections. He advised NMED to consider reopening comment.
iw: Permit comment record, mostly pro-project, under investigation

t: Mayes hears data center complaints at Mesa town hall, floats community vote
b: Mayes said she would back a law requiring a community vote on data centers and that Prop. 207 does not stop her from filing a nuisance suit. Many speakers focused on the Ahwatukee campus. She promised another town hall there.
iw: Pressure for a state pause or local votes

t: Mayes asks regulators to investigate whether APS customers subsidized data centers
b: Citing an outside analysis alleging $587 million in power costs shifted to other customers, Mayes urged a public probe before APS's $608.7 million increase is approved. APS and the Corporation Commission dispute the analysis.
iw: Could delay or shrink rate decisions tied to large users

t: Phoenix posts early-morning inspectors at Ahwatukee data center site after complaints
b: The city said it would station inspectors before legal start times and secured contractor commitments to cut noise, such as moving truck traffic and limiting early deliveries. Construction hours return to 7 a.m.-7 p.m. weekdays on Oct. 16.
iw: Added enforcement on one project, no change to its approval

t: Utah State survey: about three-quarters of residents oppose new data centers
b: A statewide August survey of nearly 900 adults found 75.8% oppose or strongly oppose building more data centers, with opposition higher nearer home. Water use was the top concern, and most were dissatisfied with state officials' handling.
iw: Broad opposition adds pressure on officials

w: Phil Weiser (D) and Victor Marx (R), governor candidates
t: Weiser and Marx outline data center views at Colorado Chamber forum
b: Weiser said data centers should meet clean-energy and water criteria, protect ratepayers, and not be forced on communities. Marx called for a common-sense approach that attracts investment, protects ratepayers and leaves decisions to local governments.
iw: Both support some guardrails; details differ

t: Tooele planning commission tables data center ordinance after four-hour hearing
b: The commission voted unanimously to table draft Chapter 34 until a data center is defined, after residents delivered a letter with more than 900 signatures. The county said the council will not accept a data center application until the chapter is complete.
iw: Local rules delayed a third time amid opposition

t: Grand Junction advances one-year moratorium on data centers of one megawatt or more
b: Council approved the first reading on Oct. 7. The pause would last up to 365 days or until code changes pass. A public hearing and final vote were scheduled for Oct. 21; the outcome was not confirmed.
iw: Low threshold, so most projects would be covered

t: Denver names 26-member working group to recommend data center rules
b: Members were picked from more than 250 applicants and include residents, unions, utilities, industry and academics. The one-year moratorium runs to May 2027 and could be extended. Officials have not ruled out a ban.
iw: Ongoing uncertainty over whether new projects will be allowed

t: Companies tied to neighboring industrial park sue Weld County over Global AI approval
b: Three companies tied to the neighboring industrial park filed in Weld District Court on Oct. 6 (case 2026CV31187) to overturn the September approval. They allege rule-bending, open-meetings violations and unenforced stop-work orders. Responses from the county and Global AI were not found.
iw: Lawsuit could overturn a key project permit

w: Biggs (R) and Hourihan (No Labels), governor candidates
t: Biggs and Hourihan debate data centers as Hobbs skips Arizona governor debate
b: Republican Andy Biggs said the state should end tax breaks and bar new centers that crowd out residents' water and power. No Labels nominee Teri Hourihan urged a roughly six-month construction pause. Gov. Hobbs did not attend.
iw: Both challengers favor tighter limits

t: Yellowstone County sues again to test legality of new data center initiative
b: Commissioners voted 3-0 to seek a court ruling on Kassi Solberg's new initiative, which would require two-thirds voter approval before data centers start or resume operations, aimed at a May 2027 vote. The county cites the Right to Compute Act.
iw: Court ruling could block the voter-approval measure

t: Blaine County adopts 182-day emergency moratorium on data center permits
b: Commissioners voted 3-0 to stop receiving, processing and approving data center permit applications for the maximum period the law allows while staff draft zoning rules. No application had been filed.
iw: Permit applications frozen for six months

t: Attorney general calls FERC review of Project Jupiter gas pipeline inadequate
b: Torrez told the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission that its environmental assessment of the 17-mile Green Chile pipeline ignores Project Jupiter's own emissions and cannot justify skipping a full impact statement. He said the pipeline exists only to fuel the project.
iw: Could slow the pipeline the project depends on

t: Mesa County commissioners approve 12-month data center moratorium
b: The unanimous vote halts acceptance and approval of data center applications in unincorporated areas while the land code is rewritten. The county had no pending applications and plans to revisit in 2027.
iw: First Western Slope county pause, year-long

t: Goldwater Institute demands Pima County rescind data center moratorium
b: The think tank says the 120-day pause breaks state law, which allows moratoria only for a shortage of essential facilities or a clear and imminent danger, and raises property-rights concerns. Supervisor Allen disputes this. Draft rules go to the planning commission Oct. 28; the pause expires in January.
iw: Legal challenge could undercut the pause

w: POWER (Protect Our Water and Energy Resources)
t: Weld County group circulates petitions for votes on Global AI data center
b: Two petitions were cleared for circulation: a referendum on commissioners' Sept. 9 approval of Global AI's Windsor project, and an initiative requiring voter approval of future data centers. Each needs 9,103 signatures. CPR reports the group is backed by a neighboring landowner.
iw: Could force a public vote on a pending project

t: Leger Fernández calls for a pause on data centers, releases 'No Blank Checks' principles
b: Rep. Teresa Leger Fernández said AI and data centers cannot regulate themselves and urged a pause in New Mexico while communities get a say, listing standards projects should meet before approval. She spoke the day Oracle's force majeure notice on Project Jupiter was reported.
iw: Another federal Democrat backs a pause

t: Montana Supreme Court reverses itself, keeps Butte data center initiative off ballot
b: The court ordered the measure onto the November ballot Sept. 22, then vacated that order two days later because ballots had already been mailed. The initiative would require two-thirds voter approval for new data centers. Organizers asked for reconsideration.
iw: Voter-approval requirement stays off the ballot for now

t: Arizona delegation demands answers on four data center proposals on federal land
b: Sens. Kelly and Gallego and Reps. Stanton, Ansari and Grijalva asked Interior for details on four proposals covering over 3,000 acres, part of 12 under BLM review in six states. They asked about environmental review, public input and water use.
iw: Adds scrutiny to fast-tracked federal-land projects

t: Boise mayor says no mega data center should proceed without statewide framework
b: McLean called a proposed data center on public land near Blacks Creek shortsighted and said none of that size should be considered until Idaho adopts a statewide framework. The Sierra Club also opposed the plan.
iw: Adds local political pressure against a very large project

t: Raton commission rejects data center moratorium 3-2 despite petition
b: Raton's City Commission voted 3-2 against a one-year moratorium after nearly 500 residents signed a petition. Opponents of the pause said city utilities and state oversight already provide safeguards. A feasibility deal with developer Atterix had ended in August.
iw: Pause rejected, though a regulating ordinance is still planned

t: Berthoud adopts 12-month moratorium on large data centers
b: Trustees voted 5-2 on Sept. 22 to pause applications for large data centers while the town studies water use, electricity demand and building standards. The mayor said the pause could be extended if the work is not finished.
iw: Large projects frozen for a year

t: Thornton adopts 12-month moratorium on data centers over 50,000 square feet
b: The council voted 5-3 for a year-long pause on new data centers over 50,000 square feet, after a 5-4 first-reading vote on Sept. 8. Expansions of existing large facilities are also barred. No applications were pending.
iw: Large projects frozen for a year

t: Tucson lowers large water user threshold, orders stricter proposals in 120 days
b: Council narrowly approved the first update to its 2025 ordinance, cutting the trigger for conservation plans from about 7.5 to 6.4 million gallons a month. Staff must return in 120 days with a proposal covering users above roughly 3.7 million gallons.
iw: Water-use rules tighten modestly for new large users

t: Yellowstone County asks legislators to refine Montana's Right to Compute Act
b: The three commissioners signed a letter saying the 2025 law keeps them from regulating Quantica's 5,000-acre project near Broadview. They asked local legislators to clarify counties' authority over data center land use.
iw: Local officials press for power to regulate large projects

t: Commerce City passes six-month data center moratorium
b: The council voted 7-1 to stop accepting new data center applications while it writes rules. Officials said the city's code has no specific standards for these facilities.
iw: Applications frozen for six months

t: BLM reviews application for 4-million-square-foot Rhea Data center near Boise
b: Rhea Data, an Arevia Power subsidiary, seeks about 3,700 acres of public land in Ada County for a 600-megawatt campus with a gas plant. BLM expects to publish a notice of intent by year-end; nothing has been approved.
iw: Early federal review of a very large project with local opposition

t: New Mexico Supreme Court rejects Project Jupiter challenges and lifts stays
b: The justices unanimously denied petitions from New Energy Economy and the Center for Biological Diversity and unpaused the air-permit proceeding and well use, without explanation. The Environment Department must still decide the permit.
iw: Legal setback for opponents; permitting resumes

w: Deb Haaland (D) and Gregg Hull (R), governor candidates
t: Haaland pledges day-one data center moratorium; Hull opposes
b: Democrat Deb Haaland said she would sign an executive order on her first day pausing new large-scale data centers until lawmakers pass an eight-point set of protections. Republican Gregg Hull opposes a moratorium, saying it signals New Mexico is closed for business.
iw: Possible statewide pause if Haaland wins in November

t: Clovis commission rejects 120-day data center moratorium 5-3
b: Commissioners voted 5-3 against pausing data center permits, saying no project was pending and a moratorium would signal Clovis was closed for business. Mayor Mike Morris, who proposed it, asked staff to keep drafting rules; an ordinance goes to the commission Nov. 5.
iw: Pause rejected, though zoning rules are coming

t: Colorado Springs council delays Project Taurus data center appeals to April 2027
b: Council voted 7-2 to postpone appeals of the 50-megawatt project near Garden of the Gods until April 13, 2027, citing noise and utility-rate questions. Four people were arrested at the contentious hearing.
iw: Project stalled about seven months with outcome uncertain

t: Pocatello council again affirms denial of AI data center on reconsideration
b: A motion to reverse failed 3-2, then the council affirmed the denial but waived the usual 12-month wait to reapply. The decision becomes official Oct. 1, after which Lex Developments has 28 days to seek judicial review.
iw: Denial reaffirmed, though a lawsuit is likely

t: Ethics Commission says Oracle disclosed $3.44 million Project Jupiter lobbying ad campaign
b: After an Ethics Commission investigation, Oracle registered and reported spending $3.44 million from January to April on ads, polling and canvassing meant to influence the Environment Department's air permit decision. The commission called it likely the largest such campaign disclosed in New Mexico.
iw: Lobbying spending now public, no penalty announced

t: Poll: nearly three-quarters of Montana voters oppose nearby data centers
b: A survey of 839 registered voters found nearly 75% oppose a data center in their city or a neighboring county, and 92% back state rules limiting effects on electricity prices. Voters split 45% to 49% on whether data centers help the economy.
iw: Broad opposition adds pressure on officials and utilities

t: Mona residents appeal Juab County permit for $10 billion data center
b: Mona Cares asked Juab County commissioners to overturn the April conditional use permit, arguing residents lacked timely notice. Commissioners said they followed state notice rules and were unsure they could cancel the permit.
iw: Administrative appeal could reopen a key permit

t: Loveland approves 12-month pause on data center land-use applications
b: Council voted 7-2 to pause land-use applications for data centers needing 10 megawatts or more; smaller facilities can still proceed. A 5-4 vote lengthened the pause from nine to 12 months, and it ends earlier if new rules are adopted.
iw: Large projects frozen for up to a year; small ones unaffected

t: Latah County adopts data center ordinance restricting groundwater cooling
b: Commissioners unanimously approved rules making data centers a conditional use in industrial zones and prohibiting consumptive groundwater use for routine cooling. No data center has been proposed in the county.
iw: Conditional approval and a groundwater cooling ban

t: Uinta County approves power-plant permit and rezoning for Prometheus data center
b: Commissioners approved a conditional use permit for on-site, off-grid power generation and rezoned a 644-acre parcel from agricultural to business industrial. The permit carries 13 conditions, including annual county inspections and road upkeep.
iw: Clears the power side of a 1.25-gigawatt campus

t: Weld County approves Global AI data center near Windsor, 5-0
b: Commissioners granted a Use by Special Review permit for a 41-acre campus on the former Carestream site. The first phase is 27.5 megawatts, with long-term plans up to one gigawatt. Most public comment at the daylong hearing opposed it.
iw: Approval of a large project, though petitions seek a vote

t: Montana interim committee advances draft bill to shield ratepayers from data center costs
b: The committee voted unanimously to carry the draft into the 2027 session. It would direct the PSC to set terms for customers of 5 megawatts or more and require financial guarantees. NorthWestern Energy criticized it.
iw: Likely cost-allocation and guarantee requirements in 2027

t: Clearfield adopts 180-day moratorium on data center development
b: The council voted 4-0 to bar data center development for six months while it studies rules, though no project is proposed. City code has no data center definition. Mayor Mark Shepherd, a MIDA board member, cited Stratos's scale.
iw: Applications frozen for six months

t: Attorney general backs challenges to Project Jupiter air permit hearing and emergency well
b: Torrez filed support for New Energy Economy and the Center for Biological Diversity, arguing the air-permit hearing was premature and the State Engineer misused an emergency well authorization. The Supreme Court denied both petitions on Sept. 17.
iw: Attorney general sided with opponents, but the court rejected the challenges

t: Hobbs rejects statewide data center moratorium, keeps push to end tax credit
b: Responding to the attorney general's call for a pause, the governor said data centers make sense in some places but must pay for themselves and not raise utility costs. Her office said she wants the tax credit ended permanently.
iw: Rejects a pause but wants the tax break ended

t: Journal poll: 65% of New Mexico voters oppose large data centers
b: An Aug. 21-28 poll of 516 likely voters found 65% oppose building large data centers and 75% support a statewide moratorium until rules are set. Opposition was higher among Democrats but a majority of Republicans also opposed.
iw: Broad bipartisan opposition adds political pressure

t: Aurora council finalizes ban on evaporative cooling in new buildings, including data centers
b: The council introduced the ordinance unanimously Sept. 14, and Denver7 reports the ban passed at the next meeting. It covers new commercial, industrial and multifamily buildings and is not retroactive, so Aurora's nine existing data centers are unaffected. The effective date is unconfirmed.
iw: Forces closed-loop cooling on new projects

t: Magellan poll: most Colorado voters oppose data centers, strongest near home
b: A survey of 1,389 registered voters found 86% oppose one near their neighborhood, 82% in their city or town and 75% elsewhere in the state. Fifty-five percent chose a ban on construction as the best path for their community.
iw: Broad opposition adds pressure on local officials

w: Alani Bankhead (D) and Seth Bodnar (I), Senate candidates
t: Montana Senate candidates Bankhead and Bodnar lay out data center positions
b: Democrat Alani Bankhead called for a moratorium on large data center development until community impacts are studied. Independent Seth Bodnar pledged to shield ratepayers and give communities the final say. The candidates agreed projects need more transparency.
iw: Moratorium and community-veto pledges in an open Senate race

t: Natrona County weighs conditions and industrial-park zoning for Prometheus data center
b: At a packed September meeting, commissioners heard Prometheus Hyperscale's plan for a roughly 1.25-gigawatt campus east of Casper. They are drafting conditions and weighing an industrial-park exemption that would bypass the state Industrial Siting Council.
iw: Zoning path and conditions still undecided

t: Mead trustees approve 12-month data center moratorium on a 4-2 vote
b: The pause prevents data center applications while staff study infrastructure, water use and setbacks. The town attorney said it does not permanently prohibit data centers. The two dissenting trustees questioned whether a full year was needed.
iw: Applications frozen for up to a year

t: Attorney General Mayes calls for statewide pause on new data center approvals
b: Citing rising energy bills and a nearly 30% cut to Colorado River supplies, Mayes urged lawmakers and the governor to halt approvals, especially hyperscale AI projects, until the state has a plan. She does not have power to impose one.
iw: First statewide official to call for a pause

w: Skull Valley Band of Goshute Indians
t: Skull Valley Goshute tribe opposes data center plans in Tooele County
b: The tribe said a hyperscale data center in Tooele County could harm the groundwater that is its sole water source. KSL tied the statement to the Army's Dugway proposal; the tribe urged county officials to oppose related zoning requests.
iw: Adds tribal water-rights opposition

w: Phil Weiser (D) and Greg Lopez (I), governor candidates
t: Colorado governor candidates split on state data center rules at debate
b: Democrat Phil Weiser backed a state law protecting community interests, clean energy standards and utility rates. Independent Greg Lopez said the jury is still out and cited water worries. Republican Victor Marx skipped the debate.
iw: Possible state regulation after the November election

w: Wyoming Minerals, Business and Economic Dev. Committee
t: Wyoming committee narrowly kills draft exempting some power generators from utility rules
b: After carrying the draft forward in June, the Minerals committee voted it down Aug. 27 as four House members opposed it. It would have let producers serving a 25-megawatt customer operate outside utility rules. Senator Rothfuss's Blockchain committee is weighing a rival version.
iw: Off-grid power exemption stalled, though rival bills continue

t: Pinal County rejects Vermaland's La Osa data center near Eloy, 4-1
b: Supervisors denied rezoning for what would have been Arizona's largest data center, on about 3,300 acres. The developer had cut the plan from 59 buildings to 11. Residents raised water, power, noise and wildlife concerns.
iw: Largest proposed Arizona campus killed by rezoning vote

t: Rep. Vasquez co-sponsors two federal data center transparency bills
b: Rep. Gabe Vasquez joined the FAIR Data Act, shielding residential and small-business customers from data center energy costs, and the Data Center Water and Energy Transparency Act, which would require usage disclosure with fines up to $20,000 a day.
iw: Backs cost-protection and disclosure mandates

t: Colfax County adopts one-year moratorium on data centers
b: Commissioners unanimously adopted Ordinance 2026-02, a one-year moratorium on data centers in unincorporated areas, citing drought and water, energy, heat and noise concerns. It does not cover Raton or other municipalities. Exact vote date needs confirming.
iw: Applications frozen for a year in unincorporated areas

t: Montana energy task force urges clear path for large loads without cost shifts
b: The 20-recommendation final report asks the state to intervene in NorthWestern's large-load tariff case and clarify how utilities serve loads like data centers, with no rate impacts or stranded costs for existing customers. Its first item is considering an appointed PSC.
iw: Wants faster service for large loads but protected ratepayers

t: Stansbury demands public accounting of Project Jupiter's water sources
b: Rep. Melanie Stansbury asked the attorney general, state engineer, environment secretary and Interstate Stream Commission for water-use, water-rights and compact-compliance details, calling for an inquiry into long-term use. She said the project's own estimates have shifted.
iw: Adds federal scrutiny of the project's water supply

t: New Mexico Supreme Court pauses Project Jupiter air permit hearing and emergency well use
b: Two unanimous orders halted the Sept. 14 air-quality permit hearing and paused an emergency well authorization, after petitions from two environmental groups. The court denied both petitions and lifted both stays on Sept. 17.
iw: Stays were temporary; permitting and well use resumed Sept. 17

t: Cox calls for MIDA overhaul and bigger governor role after Stratos backlash
b: Gov. Cox called for changes to the agency that approved Stratos, including a larger role for his office. MIDA said it had paused work on Stratos during litigation, while developer Kevin O'Leary said the project is full steam ahead.
iw: Signals tighter oversight of fast-track approvals

t: Hualapai Tribe moves to bar hyperscale data centers on its reservation
b: The council passed a resolution opposing hyperscale data centers, which KJZZ describes as a moratorium. It cites Colorado River shortages and says no developer may use tribal resources without the tribe's free, prior and informed consent.
iw: Closes a large reservation, but no project was proposed

t: Wyoming primary: Barlow wins governor nomination, moratorium backer Bien loses
b: State Sen. Eric Barlow, who says communities should decide on data center proposals, won the Republican nomination. Brent Bien, who promised a moratorium, lost. WyoFile found no sign that anti-data-center positions won local races in the southeast.
iw: A statewide pause pledge failed to win the nomination

w: Third Judicial District Court (Judge James Kaste)
t: Judge dismisses residents' challenge to Uinta County permits for Prometheus data center
b: Three residents alleged unadvertised meetings and undisclosed family ties between officials and the developer. The judge dismissed the petition because they missed a response deadline and did not show personal harm. One petitioner had dropped out earlier.
iw: Legal challenge to the county permits ended

t: Colorado Springs mayor sets 'community-first' standards for data centers
b: The city page says data centers will not be approved by default. Large projects must pay for new electric infrastructure and reserved capacity, show water availability, limit neighborhood impacts, and keep public hearings. It is a policy statement, not an ordinance.
iw: Higher bar for approval and cost responsibility

w: Interim Science, Technology and Telecom Committee
t: Interim committee hears first pitch for statewide data center moratorium
b: Reps. Micaela Lara Cadena and Angelica Rubio told the interim committee in Socorro they will introduce a statewide moratorium in January, with its definition and length still open. Republican members urged a study of job and economic effects first.
iw: Statewide pause gets its first hearing, with GOP resistance

t: Douglas County approves $19.3 million tax rebate for Parker data center
b: Commissioners voted unanimously to rebate the county's share of business personal property tax for a 22.5-megawatt Flexential facility over 35 years. Every public commenter opposed it. The company says it will create 16 jobs.
iw: Long county tax break in a state with no state incentive

t: Judge rules Yellowstone County data center initiative missed signature deadline
b: The judge held the deadline passed July 13, not Aug. 12 as organizers were first told, so the voter-approval measure stays off the November ballot. Organizers had gathered roughly 15,000 signatures against about 16,600 needed.
iw: Voter-approval measure blocked for Quantica's Broadview project

t: Aurora council rejects six-month data center moratorium on a 6-5 tiebreak
b: The mayor broke a tie against the pause. Council instead directed the city manager to draft standards within 35 days, including a possible ban on evaporative cooling and buffer zones near neighborhoods.
iw: Pause rejected, though new standards are coming

t: Tucson adopts first data center rules, requiring rezoning and half-mile buffers
b: The 6-1 vote covers facilities over 25,000 square feet or 20 megawatts. They need council-approved rezoning, no potable water for cooling, and a half-mile buffer from homes and schools. Staff will study a possible ban. Effective Sept. 4.
iw: Council discretion and large buffers raise hurdles

t: Gilbert planning commission backs strict data center rules; council vote pending
b: The recommendation would limit data centers to industrial zones, require a 650-foot setback from homes, and ban drinking water and open-loop evaporative cooling. Council held a study session in August and the vote slipped from September; reports differ on whether it is now Nov. 12 or December.
iw: Large setback and potable-water ban if adopted

t: Sanpete County approves six-month data center moratorium
b: Commissioners approved a six-month moratorium on new data center development at their Aug. 4 meeting, giving the county time to draft land-use rules. The county had no ordinance covering data centers; planners began discussing rules in May.
iw: New applications frozen for six months

t: Coeur d'Alene council opposes approving data centers until study is complete
b: Council unanimously adopted Resolution 26-065 opposing construction, expansion or approval of data centers within city limits until further analysis and policy review. Proposals would still receive due process. No data centers operate in the city.
iw: Signals denial of near-term approvals in the city

t: Heinrich introduces GRID Savings Act making large data centers pay for grid upgrades
b: The Senate Energy committee's top Democrat introduced a bill directing FERC to make hyperscale users, 150 megawatts or more, fund the grid upgrades they require. Heinrich said he is not a fan of the moratorium approach because it could push projects to places with weaker standards.
iw: Developers would bear grid-upgrade costs; he opposes moratoria

t: Montana state senator says her first 2027 bill request would ban large data centers
b: In an op-ed, Democratic Sen. Ellie Boldman said she has filed a draft request to ban large-scale data centers statewide and will not compromise. Draft requests have no legal effect until a bill is introduced.
iw: Proposed statewide ban faces a long road in the 2027 session

t: Bannock County adopts 180-day moratorium on data center permit applications
b: Emergency Ordinance 2026-02 pauses applications in unincorporated areas from July 30 through Jan. 26, 2027 while staff draft a standalone ordinance. It does not apply to Pocatello, where a separate project is under city review.
iw: Applications frozen for six months in a county with strong power resources

t: Utah regulators hear opposition to Tooele Valley data center discharge permit
b: At a July 27 hearing, residents opposed a state permit that would let the Tooele Valley project, which includes a 500-megawatt data center, discharge up to 250,000 gallons of wastewater daily toward Great Salt Lake wetlands. No decision had been issued as of mid-August.
iw: Key discharge permit faces organized opposition

t: Sierra County adopts 18-month data center moratorium after Spaceport proposal
b: Commissioners unanimously turned a resolution opposing large data centers into an 18-month moratorium on July 21, after residents protested a solar-powered data center proposed at Spaceport America. A petition had gathered 408 signatures.
iw: Applications frozen for 18 months

t: Lochbuie approves five-year data center moratorium, longest in Colorado
b: The board voted 6-1 to stop accepting or reviewing applications for new or expanded data centers. The mayor called it proactive, since no developer had approached the town.
iw: Five-year pause, the longest in Colorado

t: Monument adopts six-month moratorium on data center applications
b: The town council voted to pause new applications while the land development code is updated. No project had applied. It is the first municipality in El Paso County to adopt a pause, a week after Woodland Park.
iw: Applications frozen for six months

t: Woodland Park adopts 18-month moratorium on data center applications
b: The ordinance halts submission, acceptance and approval of data center applications in the city while staff draft standards. A councilmember said no data center proposal existed and the code does not address the use.
iw: Long pause, though no project was proposed

t: Pocatello council upholds denial of AI data center on former Hoku site, 4-1
b: Council voted 4-1 to affirm the hearing examiner's decision on the $2.6 billion project. The developer filed for reconsideration July 29. The city is updating its zoning code to address data centers, which staff said could take up to 18 months.
iw: Large project stays blocked, with reconsideration or court review possible

t: Sandpoint council directs staff to define data centers for future city ban
b: Council voted unanimously to have staff propose a definition of data center for an ordinance that would prohibit the use within city limits. Councilor Pam Duquette brought the idea. No ban has been adopted.
iw: Possible city ban if an ordinance follows

w: Commissioner of Public Lands Stephanie Garcia Richard
t: Land commissioner again denies Project Jupiter gas pipeline across state trust land
b: Commissioner Stephanie Garcia Richard rejected Energy Transfer's request to reconsider her March denial of rights-of-way for a 0.6-mile stretch of the 17-mile pipeline, citing emissions and water strain. Oracle said the project remains on schedule.
iw: Blocks part of the gas supply route for the project

t: Larimer County extends data center application pause to February 2027
b: Commissioners lengthened the pause on new applications in unincorporated areas while staff draft land-use rules. A county survey found about 94% of respondents opposed data centers locally.
iw: Applications frozen for about seven more months

t: Attorney general opens investigation into fraudulent pro-Project Jupiter comments
b: Raúl Torrez began an investigation after residents in three cities said their names were used on comments supporting the project's air permit without consent, after canvassers in Project Jupiter shirts approached them. Some elected officials said their names were also misused.
iw: Casts doubt on public support cited for the air permit

t: Missoula County adopts one-year data center moratorium outside city limits
b: Commissioners voted unanimously for interim zoning that pauses new or expanded data centers through July 8, 2027, extendable once. The county attorney said it has no authority to ban them permanently. An application already filed was not covered.
iw: Year-long freeze on new and expanded projects in the county

t: Gianforte signs Trump's Ratepayer Protection Pledge for data centers
b: The governor said the pledge commits data center companies to pay the full cost of their energy and infrastructure. The pledge is voluntary, and the elected Public Service Commission, which sets utility rates, is not bound by it.
iw: Signals developers will be expected to pay their own way

t: Grand County adopts 180-day pause on data center applications
b: Commissioners voted unanimously on July 7 for a temporary regulation while permanent standards are written. No applications were pending. Staff said a mid-scale data center could need two to four times the county's yearly electricity use.
iw: New applications frozen for six months

t: Broomfield adopts 18-month moratorium on data centers of 10 megawatts or more
b: The council voted unanimously to bar new or expanded facilities at that size through December 2027, or until regulations pass. Existing centers are unaffected.
iw: Long pause on new projects of meaningful size

t: Bonner property owner withdraws support for Krambu data center after opposition
b: The industrial park's manager withdrew his signature from the special exception application after hearing public concerns, halting a 7-megawatt first phase that could grow to 29. The county moratorium would not have covered the filed application.
iw: Opposition cost a proposed project its site

w: Reps. Chávez, Lara Cadena, Rubio and Sen. Hamblen
t: Four Democratic lawmakers plan statewide data center moratorium bill for 2027
b: Four Democratic legislators said they will push in the 2027 session for a pause on new large-scale data centers until rules cover water, energy and other impacts, paired with a bill to close the microgrid loophole. Legislation has not been drafted.
iw: Possible first statewide pause, still only a plan

t: Phoenix council vacates easements for Ahwatukee data center despite resident objections
b: The 8-1 vote on routine easements for Menlo's five-building campus came as neighbors urged a delay. Officials said the site was already zoned and exempt from Phoenix's newer data center rules, and that the vote did not approve the project.
iw: Clears a step for a project already entitled

t: Wyoming PSC rejects Anschutz request to treat Carbon County power project as non-utility
b: The commission declined to declare that a direct power-to-customer project on the Overland Trail Ranch is not a public utility, which would have carved it out of Rocky Mountain Power's territory. Developers have eyed such projects for data centers.
iw: Limits one route for data centers to buy off-grid power

t: Santa Fe County adopts 18-month moratorium on data centers over one megawatt
b: Commissioners voted unanimously June 30 to pause permits for data centers using one megawatt or more while staff write rules on water, energy and noise. The threshold was cut from 100 megawatts. No project was pending.
iw: Permits frozen for 18 months at a very low threshold

t: Logan adopts 180-day moratorium on data centers and data center power plants
b: The municipal council voted unanimously on June 30 to stop accepting or approving applications while staff study rules. The pause runs to Dec. 30. Draft rules would cap standalone sites at about eight acres and bar hyperscale facilities; they need further votes.
iw: Applications frozen for six months

t: Polis says Colorado needs data centers if rates and water use are protected
b: In an on-stage Axios interview at the Aspen Ideas Festival, the governor said data centers are needed if they lower utility rates and fit water use. He said the backlash is aimed more at AI itself than at the facilities.
iw: Governor open to projects that meet conditions

t: Data center backlash helps oust Senate President Adams and two Box Elder commissioners
b: Senate President Stuart Adams, who chaired MIDA's board, lost his June 23 primary to critic Stephanie Hollist. Box Elder commissioners Lee Perry and Boyd Bingham, who backed the Stratos agreements, also lost. Perry said his vote cost him the seat.
iw: Shows the political cost of backing mega-projects

t: Cache County adopts 180-day moratorium on data centers
b: The council voted 6-0 on June 23, with one member absent, to stop reviewing data center and related power applications in unincorporated areas. No developer interest was known. Staff will weigh new standards or a prohibition.
iw: Applications frozen for six months

t: Montana Democrats adopt two-year data center moratorium plank at convention
b: Delegates voted at the June 20 state convention to support a two-year moratorium on data center projects as a party platform plank. The plank is a political position, not law.
iw: A major party now backs a statewide pause

t: Hobbs vetoes bill letting referendum petitioners withdraw, tied to Marana data center fight
b: HB 2873 would have let citizens withdraw referendum petitions before a vote. Opponents said it targeted Marana residents challenging a data center rezoning. Hobbs's veto letter cited pending litigation. A developer's lobbyist had backed the bill.
iw: Developer-backed bill blocked

w: Utah Legislature Economic Development Interim Committee
t: Utah interim committee opens bill file to define large data centers
b: The Economic Development and Workforce Services Interim Committee voted unanimously to start a bill defining large-scale data centers in state code. Chair Sen. Ann Millner said hearings would follow. Other lawmakers are drafting environmental-review and incentive bills.
iw: Rule-writing begins; outcome unknown

t: Uinta County unanimously approves permit for Prometheus Hyperscale data center near Evanston
b: The conditional use permit covers a 506-acre campus planned at 1.25 gigawatts. Its 15 conditions include annual public water-use reporting for 10 years, noise and lighting limits, and construction starting within five years.
iw: Major county permit granted, with transparency conditions

t: Box Elder County adopts 180-day data center moratorium, exempting Stratos
b: Commissioners voted unanimously on June 10 to pause new data centers and their power plants on unincorporated land. Stratos is exempt because MIDA governs it. Critics called the move too late; the county is drafting land-use rules.
iw: New applications frozen six months, though Stratos is exempt

t: Socorro County adopts one-year data center moratorium
b: Commissioners voted unanimously on June 9 to bar data centers and related infrastructure on unincorporated land for a year and start an advisory committee on rules. It followed months of opposition to a 10,000-acre solar-powered data center plan with New Mexico Tech.
iw: Applications frozen for a year

t: Longmont bans hyperscale data centers above a power threshold
b: The council voted 6-1 to ban data centers whose peak demand reaches 5% of regional grid capacity or 100 megawatts, whichever is lower (about 70 MW). No project of that size had been proposed in the city.
